description: The telematics ECU shall boot up and be operational within 5 seconds after ignition ON.
The telematics ECU shall enter low-power sleep mode within 30 seconds after ignition OFF.
The telematics ECU shall support a watchdog timer to detect and recover from software hangs within 2 seconds.
The telematics ECU shall perform a power-on self-test (POST) at every startup and report results.
The telematics ECU shall support over-the-air (OTA) firmware updates for all onboard software components.
The OTA update mechanism shall support differential (delta) updates to minimize download size.
The telematics ECU shall verify firmware integrity using SHA-256 checksum before applying an OTA update.
The telematics ECU shall support rollback to the previous firmware version if an OTA update fails.
The telematics ECU shall notify the backend server of OTA update status (success/failure/rollback).
The telematics ECU shall support 4G LTE Cat-1 cellular connectivity as the primary communication channel.
The telematics ECU shall support automatic fallback to 2G/3G when 4G LTE is unavailable.
The telematics ECU shall support Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n for local connectivity and diagnostics.
The telematics ECU shall support Bluetooth 5.0 BLE for short-range device communication.
The telematics ECU shall support GNSS (GPS + GLONASS) for vehicle positioning with accuracy ≤ 2.5 meters CEP.
The telematics ECU shall support simultaneous cellular and GNSS operation without mutual interference.
The telematics ECU shall buffer telemetry data locally when cellular connectivity is lost and transmit upon reconnection.
The local data buffer shall support a minimum of 72 hours of telemetry data storage.
The telematics ECU shall communicate with vehicle ECUs via CAN 2.0B at 500 kbps.
The telematics ECU shall support CAN-FD communication at up to 5 Mbps data rate.
The telematics ECU shall support at least 2 independent CAN bus interfaces.
The telematics ECU shall support UDS (ISO 14229) diagnostic protocol over CAN.
The telematics ECU shall support OBD-II PID reading for standard vehicle parameters.
The telematics ECU shall decode DBC-defined CAN messages for vehicle signal extraction.
The telematics ECU shall support configurable CAN message filtering to reduce processing overhead.
The telematics ECU shall collect and transmit vehicle speed data at a minimum rate of 1 Hz.
The telematics ECU shall collect and transmit engine RPM data at a minimum rate of 1 Hz.
The telematics ECU shall collect and transmit fuel level data at a minimum rate of 0.1 Hz.
The telematics ECU shall collect and transmit odometer reading at a minimum rate of 0.1 Hz.
The telematics ECU shall collect and transmit engine coolant temperature at a minimum rate of 0.5 Hz.
The telematics ECU shall collect and transmit battery voltage at a minimum rate of 0.5 Hz.
The telematics ECU shall collect and transmit DTC (Diagnostic Trouble Codes) upon detection.
The telematics ECU shall timestamp all collected telemetry data using UTC with millisecond precision.
The telematics ECU shall transmit telemetry data to the backend server using MQTT protocol.
The MQTT connection shall use TLS 1.2 or higher for data encryption in transit.
The telematics ECU shall support configurable MQTT topic structure for data routing.
The telematics ECU shall support MQTT QoS level 1 (at-least-once delivery) for critical data.
The telematics ECU shall support MQTT QoS level 0 (at-most-once delivery) for non-critical streaming data.
The telematics ECU shall support configurable telemetry upload intervals (range: 1 second to 24 hours).
The telematics ECU shall compress telemetry payloads using gzip before transmission when payload exceeds 1 KB.
The telematics ECU shall support real-time vehicle tracking with position updates at a configurable rate (1-10 Hz).
The telematics ECU shall support geofence definition (circular and polygonal) with entry/exit event triggers.
The telematics ECU shall generate an alert event when the vehicle enters or exits a defined geofence.
The telematics ECU shall support a minimum of 100 simultaneously active geofences.
The telematics ECU shall calculate and report trip distance based on GNSS data.
The telematics ECU shall detect and report vehicle idle events (engine ON, speed = 0 for configurable duration).
The telematics ECU shall detect harsh braking events (deceleration exceeding configurable g-force threshold).
The telematics ECU shall detect harsh acceleration events (acceleration exceeding configurable g-force threshold).
The telematics ECU shall detect sharp cornering events (lateral g-force exceeding configurable threshold).
The telematics ECU shall integrate a 3-axis accelerometer with a range of ±16g and sampling rate ≥ 100 Hz.
The telematics ECU shall integrate a 3-axis gyroscope for vehicle orientation detection.
The telematics ECU shall detect potential crash events based on accelerometer impact signature and trigger an emergency alert.
The crash detection alert shall include GPS coordinates, timestamp, impact severity, and vehicle ID.
The telematics ECU shall support remote door lock/unlock commands from the backend server.
The telematics ECU shall support remote engine immobilization command with safety interlocks (only when vehicle speed = 0).
The telematics ECU shall support remote horn and light activation for vehicle location.
The telematics ECU shall authenticate all remote commands using digital signatures before execution.
The telematics ECU shall acknowledge remote command execution within 5 seconds of receipt.
The telematics ECU shall log all received remote commands with timestamp and execution status.
The telematics ECU shall support remote vehicle diagnostics request from the backend server.
The telematics ECU shall support remote configuration parameter updates (e.g., upload interval, geofence definitions).
The telematics ECU shall use a secure boot mechanism to prevent unauthorized firmware execution.
The telematics ECU shall store cryptographic keys in a hardware security module (HSM) or secure element.
The telematics ECU shall support X.509 certificate-based mutual authentication with the backend server.
The telematics ECU shall encrypt all stored sensitive data (keys, credentials) using AES-256.
The telematics ECU shall support certificate rotation and revocation mechanisms.
The telematics ECU shall implement intrusion detection for CAN bus anomaly monitoring.
The telematics ECU shall disable debug interfaces (JTAG, UART) in production firmware.
The telematics ECU shall comply with UNECE WP.29 R155 cybersecurity regulations.
The telematics ECU shall support firmware signing with RSA-2048 or ECDSA-P256 digital signatures.
The telematics ECU operating temperature range shall be -40°C to +85°C.
The telematics ECU shall withstand vibration per ISO 16750-3 for vehicle-mounted electronics.
The telematics ECU enclosure shall meet IP67 ingress protection rating.
The telematics ECU shall operate with input voltage range of 9V to 32V DC (12V/24V vehicle systems).
The telematics ECU shall include reverse polarity protection on the power supply input.
The telematics ECU shall include transient voltage suppression (TVS) for load dump protection per ISO 7637-2.
The telematics ECU quiescent current in sleep mode shall be ≤ 5 mA.
The telematics ECU peak power consumption shall not exceed 5W during normal operation.
The telematics ECU shall comply with EMC requirements per CISPR 25 Class 5.
The telematics ECU shall comply with ESD requirements per ISO 10605.
The telematics ECU PCB shall use a minimum of 4-layer stackup for signal integrity and EMI control.
The telematics ECU application software shall be based on a real-time operating system (RTOS) or embedded Linux.
The telematics ECU software shall implement a modular architecture with clearly defined API boundaries between components.
The telematics ECU shall support a task scheduler capable of managing at least 20 concurrent tasks.
The telematics ECU shall implement software-based fault management with automatic service restart on failure.
The telematics ECU shall log all software exceptions and system errors to non-volatile storage.
The telematics ECU shall support remote log retrieval for diagnostics and debugging.
The telematics ECU shall support A/B partition scheme for safe firmware updates.
The telematics ECU bootloader shall validate firmware image signature before booting.
The telematics ECU shall maintain a persistent update history log (last 10 updates minimum).
The telematics ECU shall support integration with fleet management platforms via REST API.
The telematics ECU shall support Protobuf serialization format for efficient data encoding.
The telematics ECU shall support JSON data format as a fallback for diagnostic and configuration messages.
The telematics ECU shall support device provisioning via a secure onboarding protocol.
The telematics ECU shall report its hardware and software version to the backend upon connection.
The telematics ECU shall provide a local diagnostic interface via USB for factory testing and configuration.
The telematics ECU shall support SIM card hot-swap without requiring a device reboot.
The telematics ECU shall support eSIM (eUICC) for remote SIM provisioning.
The telematics ECU shall undergo hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing for all CAN interface functions.
The telematics ECU shall pass all functional tests defined in the system verification plan before production release.
The telematics ECU software unit tests shall achieve a minimum of 80% code coverage.
The telematics ECU shall support automated regression testing via a CI/CD pipeline.
The telematics ECU shall pass environmental stress screening (ESS) including thermal cycling and vibration.
The telematics ECU GNSS module shall achieve a cold-start time-to-first-fix (TTFF) of ≤ 35 seconds.
The telematics ECU GNSS module shall achieve a hot-start TTFF of ≤ 2 seconds.
The telematics ECU shall support dead reckoning using IMU data when GNSS signal is lost (e.g., tunnels).
The telematics ECU shall support multi-constellation GNSS (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou).
The telematics ECU shall support assisted GPS (A-GPS) for faster position acquisition.
The telematics ECU shall filter GNSS outliers and apply Kalman filtering for smooth trajectory reporting.
The telematics ECU shall support speed data fusion from GNSS and CAN vehicle speed sensor for improved accuracy.
The telematics ECU shall report heading (bearing) derived from GNSS or IMU data.
The telematics ECU shall report altitude data from GNSS with accuracy ≤ 10 meters.
